plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own), so bidding higher than my value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities where I'd have won at a price below my value. With a value of $27, I should bid exactly $27 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade the bid up or down. I will bid my true value of $31.

This is a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), which is strategically similar to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do - it maximizes expected profit. Since my value is $20, I should bid exactly $20. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids (profitable), and lose when others value it more (avoiding overpayment).
